clue.text: Stupid member one found in drunkard's embrace

indicators.note: the drunkard's embrace wraps around the other pieces, so his word holds them inside

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker
MP is a Member of Parliament
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A foolish politician has turned up in the arms of a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumpish describes someone heavy, dull and slow-witted, close to stupid.

clue.text: Little girl takes Bill's flowers

parts.note: Lil is a short form of a girl's name such as Lilian
AC (account) is a bill, so Bill's gives ACS

explanation.surface: A small girl takes the flowers that belong to Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilacs are shrubs with scented purple or white blossom.

clue.text: Man is Nature's only one, sang Lady Psyche

definitions.text: Man is Nature's only one, sang Lady Psyche

parts.words: Man is Nature's only one, sang Lady Psyche
parts.note: Lady Psyche in Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida sings that man is Nature's sole error; the clue asks for that word

explanation.surface: A line of song from an operetta about men.
explanation.walkthrough: In Princess Ida, Lady Psyche's song tells of an ape who aspired to be a man, with the refrain that man is Nature's sole blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The song calls man Nature's only blunder, an error on Nature's part.

clue.text: Bury about to receive Smith with medal, we hear

indicators.note: the words for bury and about take in Smith's initials between them

parts.note: to inter is to bury
re means about or concerning
F. E. Smith, Lord Birkenhead, was a famous lawyer and politician known by his initials

explanation.surface: A burial is arranged for a decorated man called Smith.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a homophone: 'medal, we hear' sounds like meddle. F. E. Smith, Lord Birkenhead, was a celebrated English lawyer and statesman known by his initials; 'to receive' puts them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Meddle, which medal sounds like, means to poke into others' affairs.

clue.text: Usher's scholastic appointment? (Poe)

parts.note: an usher was once a junior schoolmaster, while Poe's Roderick Usher is head of his family's mansion

explanation.walkthrough: Old schools called an assistant teacher an usher; Poe's tale 'The Fall of the House of Usher' makes Roderick the man in charge of the House of Usher.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher in charge of a boarding house at school, and Roderick Usher as owner of his House.

clue.text: Joins the Specials without a disturbance

indicators.note: the letters of the word Specials, minus an A, are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A band called the Specials link up with no trouble at the gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' takes the A out of SPECIALS; 'disturbance' shuffles the remaining SPECILS into SPLICES.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice ropes or film is to join them end to end, so splices means joins.

clue.text: Bribe in this way, quietly

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A quiet back-hander is handed over like this.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a small concession given to placate someone, a kind of bribe.

clue.text: Ex-king after a while

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A former king returns after some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, once some time has passed.

clue.text: Letter from Greece opposing wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against, opposing

explanation.surface: A letter sent from Greece objects to some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Step taken not heartless, though harsh

parts.note: a stride is a long step

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of not is removed

explanation.surface: Someone takes a step without unkindness, though it seems harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and grating, harsh to hear.

clue.text: Judgment summons to help one make one's contract?

definitions.text: to help one make one's contract?

explanation.surface: A court summons might help someone fulfil a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the declarer's final card of the trump suit can be what lets them make the contract they bid.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet call that wakes the dead on Judgment Day; and in bridge, a final trump card that wins a needed trick.

clue.text: He perseveres on the Moselle

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps at it lives beside a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps trying never gives up; Trier is an ancient German city standing on the Moselle river.

clue.text: Honour and manner Moriarty once had

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes's enemy once had distinction and style.
explanation.walkthrough: Professor Moriarty, Holmes's foe, was a mathematics professor, and a professorship is called a chair; the definition stands for what he held.
explanation.definitionFit: A university professorship is known as a chair, which the fictional Professor Moriarty once held.

clue.text: Enclosed in her ends perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the words in her ends as one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Something sealed up at its far ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enshrined is set within a shrine, so it is enclosed and protected.

clue.text: Don't go round holding the toy

indicators.note: the word for don't go goes round the word for holding

parts.note: stop means don't go
pinning means holding fast

explanation.surface: Instructions to stop circling while grasping a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is a child's toy that whirls on its point.

clue.text: Nothing in particular for a Lambeth girl in production

indicators.note: the girl is placed in the word for production, cutting it open

parts.note: generation is the act of producing something
Liza of Lambeth is W. Somerset Maugham's first novel, about a girl from that London district

explanation.surface: A theatre production lacks specifics about a London girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth is a working-class district of south London, home of Maugham's heroine Liza. 'Nothing in particular' wittily describes a sweeping statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad statement with no specifics deals with nothing in particular.

clue.text: Assiduous in upsetting Evita about wine

indicators.note: the jumbled Evita goes about the wine, holding it inside
upsetting tips the letters of Evita into a new order

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep-red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Someone diligent in staging Evita needs wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns the musical's title into ATIVE, and 'about' wraps that round the wine. Tent is an old name for a sweet red Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Assiduous means diligent and careful, paying close heed.

clue.text: Use a point on the mine surface for anchorage

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
the pithead is the top of a mine shaft at ground level

explanation.surface: Use a sharp tip on the surface at the colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: SPITHEAD is the stretch of water off Portsmouth where the Royal Navy anchored its fleet. 'Use' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spithead is a famous roadstead in the Solent where ships lie at anchor.

clue.text: Calvin's doctrine — spread it in Eton for a change

indicators.note: the words spread it in Eton are to be changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Calvinist teaching is spread at Eton for once.
explanation.definitionFit: John Calvin taught that God has foreordained who will be saved, a doctrine of fate decided in advance.

clue.text: Reveal letters, say, about electoral system

indicators.note: the two letters spelt out go about the electoral system, enclosing it

parts.note: ex is the spelling of the letter X
ess is the spelling of the letter S
PR is proportional representation

explanation.surface: Disclose correspondence on how votes are counted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters, say' means letters as spelt out in words, here X and S; 'about' has them surround the voting system.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a feeling is to make it known, to reveal it.

clue.text: Head holds sanctimonious, view

indicators.note: the word for head holds the other word inside it

parts.note: onion is old slang for the head
pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A leader takes a holier-than-thou position.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view one holds on something.

clue.text: Inclined to be thin, man

parts.note: lean means thin
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man disposed to slimness.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaned means sloped or tilted, so inclined.

clue.text: Game to end with the Cresta, for instance

parts.note: a tip is the end of something
and means together with
the Cresta Run is a famous toboggan run at St Moritz, so it is an example of a run

explanation.surface: A game to finish off with tobogganing in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip-and-run is an informal cricket game in which the batter must run whenever the bat touches the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-and-run is a casual form of cricket played in parks and gardens.

clue.text: Constituent of explosive which might be inert

indicators.note: might be shows the letters of inert could be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ingredient of a bomb that might be harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a key ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Clamour for Northern French Department

parts.note: the Oise is a department of northern France

explanation.surface: A protest over a northern French region.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud racket or din.

clue.text: Note opening result

parts.note: E is a musical note
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A note on an opening outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or result can be called the event, as in 'in the event'.

clue.text: 25 dn the island state processed into food

parts.note: the answer to 25 down is a fruit
RI is Rhode Island, the US state

indicators.note: processed means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Nuts from an island state are processed into food.
explanation.walkthrough: '25 dn' points to the down answer, and 'processed' rearranges the state abbreviation with 'into' to give RITION after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is nourishment, the food a body takes in.

clue.text: 25 ac's first fruit often bolted

explanation.surface: The first fruit from a diet often eaten quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three letters of 25 across give this word; it is also a fruit, and the threaded metal piece that goes on a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel in a hard shell is a fruit, and the threaded metal fitting screwed onto a bolt shares the name.

clue.text: Girl's in ecstasy? Don't agree

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so Di's gives the letters DIS
sent is old slang for thrilled, carried away

explanation.surface: A girl's thrilled but someone won't go along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to differ in opinion, to refuse to go along.

clue.text: Smartened up the disorderly deer pen

indicators.note: disorderly signals that the letters of deer pen are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tidied the messy enclosure where deer are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds preen their feathers to tidy them, so preened means made oneself neat.
